items.title: Theorem 11.1.1 (2017: 11.1), the tangent functor on $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$

book.label: §11.1, Theorem 11.1.1, p. 521 (2017: Theorem 11.1, p. 375)
book.statement: The tangent functor $T : \mathcal{EP} \to \mathcal{EP}$ induces a functor $T : \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1}) \to \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ by $[X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y] \mapsto [TX \xleftarrow{TF} TA \xrightarrow{T\Phi} TY]$, compatible with $i : \mathcal{EP} \to \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$.

lean.statement: A refinement $H$ of diagrams gives the refinement $TH$ of the tangent diagrams, so `tangentFunctor` is well defined on classes; it preserves identities and composition, $T(i(\Phi)) = i(T\Phi)$, and it maps generalized isomorphisms to generalized isomorphisms. The comparison functor `wfpLift` $C \to X \times_Y Z$ of a pair of functors and a natural transformation gives $T(A \times_Y B) \to TA \times_{TY} TB$, an equivalence by two out of three.

items.title: Definition 11.1.3 (2017: 11.1), faces in the ep-groupoid sense

book.label: §11.1, Definition 11.1.3, p. 523 (2017: Definition 11.1, p. 377)
book.statement: A face of $|X|$ is the closure of a connected component of $\{d_{|X|} = 1\}$; a face of $X$ is the full subcategory $X_\theta$ over a face $\theta$; $X$ is face structured if it is tame and every $z$ lies in exactly $d_{|X|}(z)$ faces of $|X|$, weakly face structured if the object M-polyfold is face structured.

notFormalized.title: Proposition 11.1.6, faces as ep-groupoids, the intersection clause and $[d]_F$
notFormalized.label: §11.1, Proposition 11.1.6, pp. 524–525 (2017: Proposition 11.2, p. 378)
notFormalized.book: For tame face structured $X$: the object and morphism sets of a face are sub-M-polyfolds with tame induced structures and the face is a tame face structured ep-groupoid; two faces meet in a face of each; a generalized isomorphism induces generalized isomorphisms $[d]_F : F \to [d]_*F$ (11.1).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: it needs the restriction of an ep-groupoid to a closed saturated sub-M-polyfold and the faces $X_\theta$ as unions of faces of the object M-polyfold. The bijection $[d]_*$ and the homeomorphisms $\theta \to [d]_*\theta$ are V11.6; whether the intersection clause holds in the generality stated is left open (Findings, Chapter 11, items 6, 8). What is missing, in order: that an ep face structured $X$ has a face structured object M-polyfold, whose faces through $x$ map onto the faces of $|X|$ through $|x|$; that $X_\theta$ is a closed saturated sub-M-polyfold (a locally finite union of object faces, locally a single face); then `subEpGroupoid` (Proposition 7.1.22) gives the ep-groupoid, and $[d]_F$ needs the restriction of equivalences to sub-ep-groupoids (2026-11-09).

notFormalized.label: §11.3, Theorem 11.3.9, p. 542 (2017: Theorem 11.7, p. 395)

notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V11.25), for the intrinsic boundary orientation. sc-diffeomorphisms preserve $T^R_xX$, $C_xX$, the reduced codimension and the boundary operation of Definition 9.3.8 (`boundaryOp_map_tangentMapOn`), and so do equivalences and the fibre inverses (`EpFunctor.isReducedBoundaryTransfer_tangentMor`, `EpFunctor.isReducedBoundaryTransfer_fibreInv`); \"$d_M(x)$ is preserved\" is read for the reduced codimension of $T_xM$, which for tame $M$ is $d_M(x)$. So Theorem 11.3.9 holds for the generalized isomorphism itself, with $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}$ = `boundaryOrientation` (Definition 9.3.10, V9.38), with no transfer hypothesis (`EPLoc.theorem_11_3_9_push_boundaryOrientation`, `EPLoc.theorem_11_3_9_pull_boundaryOrientation`).
